claims.actor: Manifest-check hook and its shared helpers
claims.claim: An edited in-root path beginning with two dots is rejected as non-relative by the shared guard and receives no immediate post-edit validation.
claims.trigger: Post-change editFlow resolves a file such as <root>/..cache/package.json under the active template root
claims.exceptions: Later shell snapshot validation can still inspect the manifest. Paths genuinely outside the root should be rejected.
claims.enforcement_effect: Potential unintended exclusion from immediate advisory enforcement, not permission to violate package rules.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Root/path helper ranges are marked implementation without registering the broader-than-parent-traversal exclusion.
General manifest checking/CPM and omitted imported props/targets do not express this path-dependent edit skip.

claims.comparison_reason: The startsWith('..') test is broader than a parent-directory component. editFlow lines174..175 exits when the helper returns null. All-three relevant effective-manifest claims omit this exception.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: Edit root/..cache/package.json to use a floating version; the immediate edit branch exits while an otherwise equivalent root/cache/package.json edit reaches validation.
claims.open_question: Does this source-proven routing exclusion count as a registrable effective constraint or only an implementation defect, and which path/tool normalization conditions matter?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Executable family: pure copied path-function probe, retaining separate subsequent-shell behavior.

claims.actor: Manifest-check hook and its shared helpers
claims.claim: The post-change hook reads project-level manifest policy from the launcher's hook directory while reading selected module adapters from the resolved active configuration root.
claims.trigger: A hook launched from template A runs against an active worktree/template B with its own decisions marker and different manifest-policy.json
claims.exceptions: No difference arises when launcher and active configuration are identical. This records policy source selection, not any actual cross-candidate package-policy difference.
claims.enforcement_effect: Potential mixed-source authority for deny/approval package feedback.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Loading lists is described without distinguishing the launcher-level policy from active-root module adapters.
Actual worktree manifest validation and static package bans/confirmation do not identify which root supplies their policy.

claims.comparison_reason: here is derived from import.meta.url (post-change22); packageRules(config) reads manifest-policy using here but facets with config. Shared resolveRoots lines60..67 can choose an active configuration different from launcher.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: A linked worktree changes its project deny list while the hook is launched by the other worktree's script. The hook reads target manifests and target module selections but the launching script's project deny list.
claims.open_question: Is the mixed-root policy selection a distinct effective authority constraint under the supported launcher/active-worktree model, or an incidental defect outside intended invocation?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Cross-artifact and executable families trace settings placeholder, resolveRoots and policy construction using isolated copied-function fixtures only.

claims.actor: Manifest-check hook and its shared helpers
claims.claim: In scan fallback mode, shell-call manifest change detection uses size and modification time rather than content, so equal-size/equal-time changes are not revalidated.
claims.trigger: Git snapshot acquisition is unavailable and an earlier scan-mode snapshot exists; manifest content changes while size and mtimeMs remain equal
claims.exceptions: First observation validates all manifests; a direct edit tool follows its separate immediate validation path. This does not claim ordinary edits usually preserve mtime.
claims.enforcement_effect: Potential condition under which shell changes escape repeat advisory inspection.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Scan fallback and state handling are described without a registered equal-metadata exclusion.
Claims concern validating changed manifests or omitted manifest kinds; neither states fallback identity is only size/time.

claims.comparison_reason: snapshot emits size:mtimeMs identifiers in fallback; shellFlow lines197..204 compares identifiers and exits when unchanged. The union's general actual-state claim does not register this narrower trigger.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: After a scan-mode checkpoint, a shell rewrites a same-length stable version to a same-length prohibited value and restores the original mtime. With no other delta, no revalidation occurs.
claims.open_question: Is this technical change-detector limitation independently normative/effective enough to register, and can the metadata-equality precondition be reproduced in an isolated fixture?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Executable-family pure snapshot/delta fixture; no candidate hook execution or source mutation.
